shorts-animados.nombre: Shorts animados de historias con giro
ejemplos: Why Perfect Railroads Don't Work
The Ancient Jar That Warned an Empire
The Job Nobody Wants in Japan
The Burglar Who Only Moved Furniture
How a Mirror Rigged a Horse Race
guion_semilla: Open in the middle of the strangest moment, in one line of 9-19 words that states the result before the cause (a man who tells an emperor to run, a law that makes firing impossible), then back up with «You see,» and tell how it came about.
Say it at about 3.2-3.6 words per second (195-215 a minute) in sentences of 10-17 words, with no filler and no questions to the viewer.
Give the hero something to lose in the first 10 seconds (a race, a job, an emperor's trust) and make everyone around him wrong and laughing at him.
Use hard numbers and objects, never adjectives: a gap every 39 feet, eight dragons, three years in a room. One fact per sentence.
Raise the stakes in steps with «Then», «Weeks later», «The next morning»; each step makes the hero look more foolish before the turn.
Hold the explanation for the last sentence: the mechanism (a pendulum, a rail that grows in heat, a law with a loophole) arrives as the reveal, in plain words.
Put one short line of dialogue inside the story so the story is not only narrated; the viewer hears a voice.
Do not ask for a like or a subscription and do not recap; end on the reveal or on the cliffhanger so the video can loop back to its first line.

explicativo-tipografico.nombre: Autosuperación y filosofía con texto en movimiento
ejemplos: cómo funciona el estoicismo moderno
hábitos para enfocarte más rápido
modelos mentales para decidir mejor
disciplina cuando no tienes ganas
guion_semilla: Open with a contrast question in two sentences: a fact everyone accepts, then «So why…?» (we have more knowledge than ever — so why are so few self-educated?). Answer it in the third sentence with a reframe of 2-4 words («Understanding is.»).
Promise the structure out loud right after the hook («Here's the exact framework.») and then label each block «Part one», «Part two»… or «First», «Second», «Third»; 3-4 blocks for 2-3 minutes.

Each block: a counter-intuitive claim («This is going to sound backwards»), one concrete everyday example (learning video editing, a walk, a phone), then one or two famous cases by name (Darwin's notebooks, Feynman's pages), then a one-line aphorism that closes it («A blank page is often a better teacher than another book»).
Speak at about 185-190 words a minute in short sentences (8-14 words), with paradox lines of 3-6 words («It's actually the opposite.», «It's just less.») after every longer explanation.
Use the first person once early as proof («This is exactly what I did when I was learning editing», «Last year, I couldn't focus for more than 20 minutes»), never as a long story.
Write in triads: three items, three adjectives, three «less»: «fast, loud, chaotic»; «less input, less switching, less noise».
End calm and anti-hype in one or two short lines («It's not viral. It's not a hack, but it works.») or a soft pointer to more; no loud call to action.
Music under the whole voice, never silence; the voice stays in front.
explicativo-tipografico.guion_fuente: Leído de 2 transcripciones reales (The Art of Becoming Dangerously Self-Educated; How to Reset Your Overstimulated Brain), 3 nov. 2026.

ensayo-documental.nombre: Ensayo documental con mapas y archivo
ejemplos: How Switzerland Engineered the Perfect Country
The Dark Truth of the Panama Canal
Why This Island Could Trigger World War 3
The Prison Break That Embarrassed an Entire Country
guion_semilla: Open on a thesis line of 3-5 words that will come back as a refrain («Information is power.») and repeat it at the end of each act, so the long video has a spine.
Tell history as a fast chronological ride (kings and the Church → the printing press → radio and television → the internet), one era per few sentences, each era ending with what changed in power.
Narrate in the first person plural and singular with on-location presence («here in America», «We're in one of those moments right now»), at about 190 words a minute in sentences of about 15 words.
Let archive speak: drop in short real clips of the period (a newsreel line, a TV announcer) between narrated sentences, then continue the sentence over it.
Carry numbers and named institutions, never vague claims: about 2 numbers a minute and every actor named (a company, a law, a regulator).
Turn with «But…» about twice a minute: each turn shows the powerful moving back in («But the elites didn't suddenly stop trying to control information»).
Build in acts of 2-4 minutes (about 17 parts in 13 minutes), each one on a map, a document or a place, and end each act on an open question that the next one answers.
Close by bringing the history to the present and to the viewer's choice, with the refrain once more; a project or sponsor mention goes at the very end, clearly as such.
ensayo-documental.guion_fuente: Leído de 1 transcripción real (The Internet Didn't Fail. It Was Taken.), 3 nov. 2026: medir más videos en su PC.

reto-narrado.nombre: Retos y viajes narrados en primera persona
ejemplos: I Took the Longest Train Ride in America
I Tested Every 1-Star Hotel
How Many Days Can I Survive an Abandoned Mall?
How Many Countries Can I Visit in 7 Days?
guion_semilla: Open in 4 words, in the moment, to the viewer («Good morning, sleepy heads.»), then restate the challenge and where the series stands in one sentence (the final day of testing the top 10 attractions).
Narrate in very short sentences (median 7 words, about 190 words a minute) in the present or just-past tense, with the clock and the place always said (a 4:00 a.m. wake-up, a connection in Phoenix).
Put a problem in the way within the first minute (a 2-hour delay that risks the concert) and solve it with self-deprecating humor («luckily, I'm really fast»).
Let other people talk: real lines from the companion, a pilot, a stranger, cut in between the narration (about every 20-40 seconds).
Count everything on screen and in words: «Number one… number two…», rankings, stamps, days, dollars (about 6 numbers a minute).
Read the sponsor inside the story at a natural beat (a delay, a wait), never as a cold block.
Score each stop and keep the running ranking, so every part ends with a verdict («We ranked Red Rocks at number seven»).
End sincere: thank the companion and the viewers in plain words, the final verdict, and «Take care, guys. See you soon.»

_canales: Canales que eligió el dueño (2 nov. 2026: «mira sus últimos 20 videos a 30 fps; la luz, el contraste, las sombras, el movimiento, los efectos, el corte, todo; transcribe cómo está escrito el guion»). Sergio baja en su equipo los últimos 20 de cada uno solo para estudiarlos, los mide a 30 cuadros por segundo y transcribe el guion; aprende la técnica, nunca usa su imagen, su voz ni sus palabras, y nunca los nombra en pantalla. «@ryan» es Ryan Trahan y «@your.nextcore» un canal de autosuperación; los videos de más de «max_minutos» (por defecto 60) se saltan: no se bajan compilaciones de horas.
